title: What Is AI?
objective: Explain what artificial intelligence is and identify a few everyday AI systems.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Artificial intelligence is the broad idea of making computer systems perform tasks that usually require human judgment, such as recognizing patterns, understanding language, or making predictions."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Artificial intelligence","flashcardId":"flashcard-ai-basics-1"},{"type":"list","items":["AI can follow rules or learn patterns from examples.","AI produces useful outputs without having human feelings or awareness.","The quality of an AI result depends on its data, design, and use."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"Key idea","text":"AI is a tool built for a task, not a human mind in a machine."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Machine learning","flashcardId":"flashcard-ai-basics-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"scenario","narrative":"A photo app groups pictures that contain dogs, suggests a search label, and improves after its developers provide more examples.","reflectionPrompt":"Which parts of this example involve recognizing patterns, and what might still go wrong?","takeaway":"The app is using an AI pattern-recognition system for a specific task; it does not understand dogs as a person does."}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Which description best matches artificial intelligence?","options":[{"id":"ai","text":"A computer system designed to perform tasks that can require human-like judgment","isCorrect":true},{"id":"internet","text":"Any device that is connected to the internet","isCorrect":false},{"id":"database","text":"A folder that stores files","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"AI describes systems designed to carry out tasks such as prediction, recognition, or language processing."}

title: Generative AI
objective: Describe how generative AI creates new text, images, audio, or code from learned patterns.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Generative AI creates a new response from patterns learned during training. It can generate text, images, audio, video, or code when a user provides an instruction."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Generative AI","flashcardId":"flashcard-generative-ai-1"},{"type":"list","items":["A prompt gives the system a task or direction.","The output is generated rather than copied from one fixed template.","Generated content still needs human review for accuracy and fit."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"watch_out","title":"Watch out","text":"A fluent answer can sound original and confident while still being wrong or unsuitable."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Training data","flashcardId":"flashcard-generative-ai-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"scenario","narrative":"A museum educator asks an AI assistant for three child-friendly descriptions of an exhibit. The assistant drafts different versions that the educator edits before publishing.","reflectionPrompt":"Why is this generative AI use helpful, and what should the educator check?","takeaway":"Generative AI can speed up drafting, but a knowledgeable person remains responsible for the final content."}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"What makes a system generative AI?","options":[{"id":"create","text":"It produces new content in response to an instruction","isCorrect":true},{"id":"store","text":"It stores every file on a computer","isCorrect":false},{"id":"connect","text":"It connects a device to Wi-Fi","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Generative AI creates content such as text, images, audio, or code from learned patterns."}

title: What Is an LLM?
objective: Explain in simple terms how a large language model generates likely text responses.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"A large language model, or LLM, is a model trained on many examples of language. It generates text by estimating what tokens are likely to come next in context."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Large language model","flashcardId":"flashcard-llm-basics-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Training teaches a model statistical patterns in language.","An LLM does not automatically know whether every statement is true.","The prompt and conversation context influence the generated response."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"Think in probabilities","text":"An LLM is very good at producing plausible language; plausibility is not the same as verified knowledge."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Next-token prediction","flashcardId":"flashcard-llm-basics-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"scenario","narrative":"When a user starts a sentence with The capital of France is, an LLM is likely to continue with Paris because that pattern appeared often in its training.","reflectionPrompt":"What does the model use to choose a continuation, and why might it still make a factual mistake?","takeaway":"LLMs generate likely continuations from patterns and context; they do not guarantee that a continuation has been checked against reality."}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"What is the basic generation process of an LLM?","options":[{"id":"predict","text":"Estimate likely next tokens from learned patterns and the current context","isCorrect":true},{"id":"search","text":"Look up every answer in a live database","isCorrect":false},{"id":"think","text":"Use human consciousness to understand the question","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"LLMs generate language from learned statistical patterns and the text currently in context."}

title: Tokens and Context
objective: Describe tokens and context windows and use that knowledge to write focused requests.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Language models process text as tokens. A token may be a whole word, part of a word, punctuation, or a space-related fragment."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Token","flashcardId":"flashcard-tokens-context-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Longer input uses more tokens and leaves less room for the response.","A context window is the amount of recent information a model can process together.","Clear, relevant context helps the model focus on the task."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"watch_out","title":"Practical limit","text":"If important details are buried in excessive or unrelated text, the response may miss them even when the model supports a large context."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Context window","flashcardId":"flashcard-tokens-context-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"worked_example","before":"Summarize this very long collection of notes and make it useful.","after":"Summarize the following meeting notes in five bullets. Keep decisions, owners, and deadlines. Ignore repeated greetings and side conversations.","annotations":["The task has a clear output format.","The relevant context is separated from the instruction.","The request removes low-value details."]}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Why should a prompt include only relevant context when possible?","options":[{"id":"focus","text":"Relevant context helps the model focus and leaves room for the requested response","isCorrect":true},{"id":"secret","text":"Unrelated text makes the model automatically more accurate","isCorrect":false},{"id":"speed","text":"Tokens determine the speed of a users internet connection","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Focused context reduces distraction and preserves context-window space for the answer."}

title: Prompt Engineering Basics
objective: Improve an AI request by stating the task, context, audience, constraints, and desired format.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Prompt engineering is the practice of designing instructions that make an AI task clear. A strong prompt gives the model enough context without burying the goal."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Prompt","flashcardId":"flashcard-prompt-basics-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Name the task and the intended audience.","Provide facts, source material, or constraints that matter.","Specify a useful format and define what success looks like."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"A prompt is a brief","text":"The model can only use the instructions and context you provide, so make the job and boundaries visible."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Constraint","flashcardId":"flashcard-prompt-basics-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"worked_example","before":"Write a post about our event.","after":"Draft a friendly 80-word announcement for new employees about Friday's AI workshop. Include the time, room, and one reason to attend. Use plain language and end with a call to register.","annotations":["The audience and purpose are explicit.","A length and style constraint guides the output.","Required facts and a desired ending reduce rework."]}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Which addition is most useful when asking AI to draft a learner announcement?","options":[{"id":"audience","text":"State who will read it, the purpose, and the required format","isCorrect":true},{"id":"vague","text":"Ask the model to make it perfect without more information","isCorrect":false},{"id":"length","text":"Add unrelated background to make the prompt longer","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Audience, purpose, relevant context, and format give the model actionable guidance."}

title: Hallucinations and Verification
objective: Recognize AI hallucinations and choose practical ways to verify important outputs.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"An AI hallucination is an output that presents invented, inaccurate, or unsupported information as if it were reliable. It can happen because the model is generating plausible language, not checking every claim."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Hallucination","flashcardId":"flashcard-hallucinations-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Treat specific names, dates, numbers, and citations as claims to check.","Compare important claims with trustworthy primary or expert sources.","Ask the model to show uncertainty, but do not treat that request as proof."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"watch_out","title":"Confidence is not evidence","text":"A polished answer and a confident tone do not demonstrate that the underlying claims are true."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Verification","flashcardId":"flashcard-hallucinations-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"scenario","narrative":"An assistant gives a detailed citation for a research paper, but the librarian cannot find the paper in the journal or library catalogue.","reflectionPrompt":"What should happen before the citation is included in a report?","takeaway":"The citation should be independently checked and removed or corrected if the source cannot be verified."}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"What is the safest first response to an AI answer containing an important unfamiliar statistic?","options":[{"id":"verify","text":"Check the statistic against a trustworthy source before relying on it","isCorrect":true},{"id":"publish","text":"Use it because the answer sounds confident","isCorrect":false},{"id":"repeat","text":"Ask the same question again and accept the second number","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Important claims should be verified independently; repeating a generation does not make it evidence."}

title: Bias and Responsible AI
objective: Identify ways bias can enter an AI system and apply basic responsible-use practices.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"AI systems can reproduce or amplify patterns in their data, labels, objectives, and surrounding processes. Bias is not only a property of the model; it can arise throughout the system."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Bias","flashcardId":"flashcard-responsible-ai-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Check whether important groups are represented in the data.","Test outcomes for different groups and look for unequal errors.","Keep human oversight for high-impact decisions and provide a way to appeal."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"Responsible use is a process","text":"Fairness, privacy, transparency, safety, and accountability need attention before and after deployment."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Human oversight","flashcardId":"flashcard-responsible-ai-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"scenario","narrative":"A hiring-screening model recommends fewer candidates from one group. The team discovers that historic hiring decisions used as labels reflected an earlier lack of representation.","reflectionPrompt":"Which questions should the team ask before using the model?","takeaway":"The team should investigate data and error patterns, involve affected stakeholders, and keep accountable human review rather than treating the recommendation as neutral."}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Which practice best supports responsible use of an AI system in a high-impact setting?","options":[{"id":"oversight","text":"Test outcomes for affected groups and keep accountable human review","isCorrect":true},{"id":"ignore","text":"Assume the system is fair because it is automated","isCorrect":false},{"id":"hide","text":"Remove all records so nobody can inspect the process","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Testing, oversight, transparency, and accountability help identify and manage harms."}

title: Evaluating AI Output
objective: Evaluate an AI response using accuracy, relevance, completeness, clarity, and safety criteria.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Evaluation turns a vague feeling about an AI response into a repeatable review. Different tasks need different criteria, but accuracy, relevance, completeness, clarity, and safety are useful starting points."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Evaluation criteria","flashcardId":"flashcard-evaluating-output-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Compare factual claims with reliable references.","Check whether the response answered the requested task and audience.","Look for missing caveats, unsafe advice, or unsupported certainty."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"Review the whole task","text":"A response can be factually correct but still fail if it omits a requirement, uses the wrong audience, or creates a safety risk."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Ground truth","flashcardId":"flashcard-evaluating-output-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"worked_example","before":"The answer looks polished, so approve it.","after":"Check each claim against the source notes, mark which requirements are met, identify omissions, and have a subject-matter reviewer assess any high-impact advice.","annotations":["Accuracy is tested against an agreed reference.","Task requirements are checked separately from style.","Risk determines whether expert review is needed."]}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Which evaluation question checks relevance?","options":[{"id":"relevance","text":"Does the response address the requested task and intended audience?","isCorrect":true},{"id":"fluency","text":"Does every sentence sound impressive?","isCorrect":false},{"id":"length","text":"Is the response longer than the prompt?","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Relevance asks whether the output serves the actual task and audience, not just whether it sounds polished."}

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
objective: Explain how retrieval-augmented generation supplies relevant sources to a language model before it answers.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"Retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG, combines search with generation. A retrieval step finds relevant content, and the language model uses that supplied context to draft a response."},{"type":"key_term","term":"RAG","flashcardId":"flashcard-rag-1"},{"type":"list","items":["A retriever searches an approved collection for relevant passages.","The passages are added to the model context as grounding material.","The final answer should still be checked for retrieval and generation errors."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"watch_out","title":"Retrieval is not a guarantee","text":"RAG can provide useful evidence, but a poor search result or a misleading source can still lead to a poor answer."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Grounding","flashcardId":"flashcard-rag-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"worked_example","before":"Ask the model to answer questions about a changing company handbook from memory.","after":"Search the current approved handbook for relevant passages, provide those passages with the question, and require the response to identify its supporting section.","annotations":["The source collection is defined.","Retrieval supplies current context.","A citation or section reference supports review."]}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"What is the role of retrieval in a RAG system?","options":[{"id":"sources","text":"Find relevant source content to provide as context for generation","isCorrect":true},{"id":"training","text":"Permanently retrain the model for every user question","isCorrect":false},{"id":"grading","text":"Replace all human review with an automatic score","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Retrieval finds relevant material for the current request; it does not necessarily change the model weights."}

title: Building a Simple AI Workflow
objective: Design a small AI-assisted workflow with clear inputs, checks, human decisions, and measurable outcomes.
lessonJson: [{"type":"paragraph","text":"An AI workflow is more than a prompt. It defines the input, transformation, output, checks, human decisions, and feedback used to improve the process."},{"type":"key_term","term":"AI workflow","flashcardId":"flashcard-ai-workflow-1"},{"type":"list","items":["Start with a bounded task and a measurable success criterion.","Keep sensitive data and permissions in the design from the beginning.","Add validation and a human handoff when errors or risks matter."]},{"type":"callout","tone":"key_idea","title":"Automate carefully","text":"A reliable workflow makes uncertainty visible and gives people a meaningful way to intervene."},{"type":"key_term","term":"Human in the loop","flashcardId":"flashcard-ai-workflow-2"}]
exampleJson: {"type":"worked_example","before":"Let AI automatically send every customer reply.","after":"Classify incoming questions, draft a response from approved help content, check for missing information and risky requests, then route uncertain cases to a support specialist before sending.","annotations":["The input and source boundary are defined.","Validation catches predictable failures.","A human handles uncertainty and high-risk cases."]}
checkpointJson: {"kind":"single_question","prompt":"Which design makes an AI workflow safer and easier to improve?","options":[{"id":"handoff","text":"Define success, validate outputs, and route uncertain cases to a person","isCorrect":true},{"id":"autonomy","text":"Remove checks so the system can act on every output","isCorrect":false},{"id":"opacity","text":"Avoid measuring results so users cannot find failures","isCorrect":false}],"explanation":"Boundaries, measures, validation, and human handoffs make failures visible and manageable."}
